cards.title: Use Quality Score Visibility to Cut Search Costs
cards.summary: Monitor per-keyword quality score in manual Search campaigns — something PMax hides — because it affects CPC and ad position and can be improved through relevance work.
cards.use_when: Optimizing existing Search campaigns for efficiency and diagnosing high CPCs.

cards.title: Set Up Demand Gen Retargeting with PMax's Winning Creative
cards.summary: Move proven PMax image and video creative into a single Demand Gen retargeting campaign so the algorithm can switch a user seamlessly between image and video ads with consolidated data.
cards.use_when: Building the image/video retargeting component of an ecommerce Google Ads structure to replace PMax's opaque retargeting.

cards.title: Segment Retargeting Audiences by Funnel Stage
cards.summary: Build distinct retargeting audiences — product page viewers, ATC non-purchasers, checkout abandoners, category viewers, all visitors, past purchasers — so you can read ROAS, spend, and clicks per audience.
cards.use_when: Configuring Demand Gen (or other retargeting) campaign audiences for an ecommerce store and needing audience-level performance reporting.

cards.title: Segment Demand Gen Reporting by Network and Optimize Creative Accordingly
cards.summary: Use Demand Gen's network/placement segmentation to see whether YouTube in-stream, Shorts, Discover, Gmail, or Display is driving results, then reallocate creative and budget to what works.
cards.use_when: Optimizing image/video retargeting creative and placement allocation for an ecommerce store running Demand Gen.

cards.title: The PMax ROAS-Floor Hack: Keep PMax as a De-Prioritized Safety Net
cards.summary: Set PMax's ROAS target far above your manual campaigns (e.g., manual at 300-400%, PMax at 600-700%) so higher manual bids win most auctions while PMax catches leftover queries and audiences.
cards.use_when: After building Standard Shopping, Search, and Demand Gen campaigns, deciding what to do with the existing Performance Max campaign.

cards.title: Set Different ROAS Targets for Incremental vs Non-Incremental Traffic
cards.summary: Apply aggressive ROAS targets to high-intent branded traffic and lower targets to non-brand acquisition, so reported performance reflects true business growth instead of funnel re-engagement.
cards.use_when: Setting campaign-level ROAS targets or evaluating whether reported Google Ads ROAS represents genuine new-customer growth for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Decide Between PMax-First and Manual Multi-Campaign Structures
cards.summary: Choose PMax alone for simplicity, or the three-component manual build (Standard Shopping + segregated Search + Demand Gen) when you have the time and expertise to scale beyond PMax's control limits.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much Google Ads campaign structure to operate for an ecommerce store, based on available time, skill, and scaling ambitions.

cards.title: The Rule of One: Anchor Each Ad and Landing Page to a Single Big Idea
cards.summary: Michael Masterson's Rule of One says compelling sales messages center on one big idea rather than stacked selling points, with evidence from 91 of the top 100 offers.
cards.use_when: Deciding the core message for a paid social ad, landing page, advertorial, or PDP before briefing creative or writing copy.

cards.title: Audit Ad and Page Copy for 'Tossed Salad' Clutter
cards.summary: Diagnose cluttered messaging that stacks unrelated selling points, then consolidate it into one reinforcing argument.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an underperforming ad, landing page, or advertorial that has accumulated multiple selling points over iterations.

cards.title: Use the Rule of One to Force a Single USP
cards.summary: A USP should be one core proposition everyone immediately understands, not nineteen competing propositions.
cards.use_when: Defining or revising the unique selling proposition for a product launch, brand campaign, or product page.

cards.title: Set Up a TikTok Business Center and Advertiser Account Cleanly
cards.summary: Create a dedicated TikTok Business Center with a business-domain email, verified advertiser account and backup payment method before spending on ads.
cards.use_when: You are launching a store's first TikTok ads and need foundational account infrastructure that supports smoother approvals and billing.

cards.title: Install the TikTok Pixel Through Shopify Partner Integration
cards.summary: Install the TikTok Pixel via partner integration and confirm core conversion events such as complete payment are tracking before launch.
cards.use_when: You are preparing a Shopify store to run TikTok conversion campaigns and need reliable purchase event tracking.

cards.title: Use the Three-Tier Campaign Pyramid for TikTok Ads
cards.summary: Structure TikTok campaigns as objective-level campaigns, experiment-level ad groups and creative-level ads to keep testing organized and scalable.
cards.use_when: You are building or restructuring a TikTok ad account for a product store and want clear separation between objectives, audiences and creatives.

cards.title: Configure a Conversion Ad Group with Broad Targeting and $50/Day
cards.summary: Set up a web-conversion ad group with pixel-based complete payment optimization, TikTok-only placement, broad demographic targeting and at least $50/day.
cards.use_when: You are creating the first TikTok conversion ad group for a store and need concrete settings and a defensible minimum budget.

cards.title: Build Three Custom Audiences, Then Lookalikes Instead of Direct Retargeting
cards.summary: Create 180-day web visitors, 30-day video completers and uploaded customer files as seeds, then use lookalike audiences in cold ad groups rather than targeting the seeds directly.
cards.use_when: You have a Shopify store with pixel traffic, video views or customer data and want to build TikTok audiences for prospecting campaigns.

cards.title: Keep Interest Targeting to Two or Three Broad Parent Categories
cards.summary: Limit TikTok interest targeting to a few broad parent categories because stacking 15+ interests raises spend and constrains the algorithm.
cards.use_when: You are setting interest targeting for a TikTok conversion ad group and are tempted to stack many detailed interests.

cards.title: Use a Four-Week Targeting Ladder to Refine Audiences Without Overspending
cards.summary: Start broad in week one and add one layer of targeting per week—basic interest, then lookalikes, then stacked winners—to gather data while controlling costs.
cards.use_when: You are launching or scaling a TikTok campaign and want a structured sequence for audience refinement instead of guessing all targeting at once.

cards.title: Apply the 3:3 Creative Testing Framework Across Hooks, Angles and CTAs
cards.summary: Test three hooks, three angles and three CTAs per product, with at least three distinct ad styles, to find converting creative combinations.
cards.use_when: You have a product to advertise on TikTok and need a structured creative testing plan rather than random video variations.

cards.title: Structure a 3:2:1 Test: Three Creatives, Two Audiences, One Objective
cards.summary: Run a first test with three distinct ad creatives, two audience types and one clear objective over three to four days for roughly $300–400 total.
cards.use_when: You are launching a first paid test for a store and need a concrete test plan with budget, duration and audience options.

cards.title: Check Core TikTok Metrics in the First 24–72 Hours
cards.summary: Use early CTR, watch time and CPM thresholds to diagnose whether a TikTok ad is failing on creative, audience or hook before spending more.
cards.use_when: You have launched a TikTok ad group and need a fast, structured read on whether to fix, kill or scale it.

cards.title: Use the Diagnostic Checklist to Separate Creative Problems from Audience Problems
cards.summary: Map specific early performance failures to the right fix: weak hook, creative transitions or audience targeting.
cards.use_when: A TikTok ad group is underperforming and you need to decide whether to change the creative or the targeting before spending more.

cards.title: Use Native Video Formats and the Five Highest-Converting Hook Patterns
cards.summary: Make TikTok ads that look like organic content using UGC, POV or tutorial formats, and open with one of five hook patterns to stop the scroll.
cards.use_when: You are creating ad creative for a store on TikTok and need formats and hook patterns that match the platform rather than TV-style ads.

cards.title: Follow the 0–35 Second Ad Structure and Technical Specs
cards.summary: Build TikTok ads in four timed sections—hook, promise, proof, CTA—and meet minimum video specs such as 9:16 and 15–35 seconds.
cards.use_when: You are scripting and producing a TikTok ad for a store and want a concrete structure and export settings.

cards.title: Build a High-Retention Ad with an Undeniable Hook and Rhythmic Editing
cards.summary: Analyze a 30M-view TikTok ad to learn how a curiosity-driven hook, promised payoff and varied clip rhythm can sustain retention.
cards.use_when: You are editing a TikTok ad for a store and want to increase watch time and rewatch rate through pacing and payoff structure.

cards.title: Edit UGC-Style TikTok Ads in CapCut with the Agency Formula
cards.summary: Use CapCut to trim hooks, apply a 4K filter, add hook text, add commercially safe music and export at 1080p with a defined workflow.
cards.use_when: You are producing TikTok ad creative in-house and need a repeatable editing workflow with specific settings.

cards.title: Use a Naming Convention and Avoid Smart Campaigns for Cleaner Testing
cards.summary: Name campaigns by product, objective and date, and toggle off smart campaigns to preserve manual control over ad group testing.
cards.use_when: You are creating TikTok campaigns for a store and need reporting clarity plus full control over testing variables.

cards.title: Meta CPM inflation and the efficiency trade-off
cards.summary: Why Meta's ad costs rise every year and what that means for how you plan creative and offers on your store's account.
cards.use_when: Planning annual ad budget, forecasting CPM/CPA inflation, or explaining to a founder why yesterday's winning creative stopped being profitable.

cards.title: Last-click reality vs. Meta's multi-touch optimization
cards.summary: Why ad-level ROAS in the UI misleads budget decisions and why you should evaluate creative at the adset level.
cards.use_when: Deciding which ads to kill or scale, or reconciling an ad's reported ROAS with actually getting spend.

cards.title: Trust the algorithm's breakdown spend distribution
cards.summary: Why breakdowns (placement, age, gender, region) rarely justify restructuring, and how incremental returns explain apparent misallocation.
cards.use_when: Tempted to launch a dedicated campaign for a placement or demographic that shows higher ROAS in a breakdown report.

cards.title: Creative-as-targeting and why broad targeting works
cards.summary: Meta's retrieval system now uses your creative to find buyers, so interest and lookalike targeting are largely obsolete.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new cold campaign or considering interest/lookalike tests instead of broad targeting.

cards.title: Consolidation beats segmentation: the campaign-level data silo
cards.summary: Why fewer campaigns generally perform better and how conversion-data splitting at the campaign level drives that.
cards.use_when: Restructuring a Meta account that has many campaigns, or deciding whether to add a new campaign or adset for a new angle or product.

cards.title: Five diagnostic questions for account structure
cards.summary: The product, margin, persona, region and creative-volume questions to answer before designing any Meta structure.
cards.use_when: Designing or restructuring a store's Meta account to match the business's products, margins and goals.

cards.title: Generic sub-$50k/month Meta structure
cards.summary: A simple, low-segmentation structure most small advertisers can run while testing concept-based creatives.
cards.use_when: Launching or cleaning up a Meta account spending under roughly $50k/month with limited creative volume.

cards.title: Budgeting the retargeting support layer
cards.summary: Treat retargeting as a capped, small support campaign and calculate its budget from audience size, frequency and CPM.
cards.use_when: Setting or auditing retargeting/DPA spend for existing customers or engaged audiences.

cards.title: Calculating daily testing budgets by back-propagation
cards.summary: Derive the daily test budget from target conversions, expected CPA and test duration instead of guessing.
cards.use_when: Setting the daily spend for a specific creative or landing-page test and deciding how long to run it.

cards.title: Choosing ABO vs CBO by conversion volume and signal
cards.summary: When to let the campaign distribute budget (CBO) versus controlling it per adset (ABO).
cards.use_when: Deciding campaign budget type for a store, especially with high AOV, low order volume, or risky product ranges.

cards.title: Segment accounts by unit economics and audience
cards.summary: When margin spread, non-overlapping personas, or high AOV/low volume make segmentation worth the added complexity.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to separate products, categories or audiences into their own campaigns despite the consolidation rule.

cards.title: Worked example: CPG brand structure with one persona and two markets
cards.summary: How a one-product, one-persona, 70%-margin CPG brand at $5M/year should structure Meta for US and AU.
cards.use_when: Designing structure for a simple consumable product with high repeat rate and few personas.

cards.title: Worked example: fashion brand with SKUs, personas and regions
cards.summary: How a 50-SKU, four-persona fashion brand at $5M/year should structure Meta across AU/NZ and UK.
cards.use_when: Designing structure for a multi-category, multi-region store with discounting and seasonal differences.

cards.title: Page caps, whitelisting and regional pages
cards.summary: How to keep running high creative volume once you hit Meta's active-ad cap per page.
cards.use_when: Scaling weekly creative output and being blocked from launching more ads on a single page.

cards.title: What media buying still controls (and what's dead)
cards.summary: Prioritize structure, concept-level adsets and customer allocation over bids, budget tweaks and interest tests.
cards.use_when: Allocating media-buyer time across an account, or deciding which levers to pull for efficiency.

cards.title: Concept definition and adset grouping rule
cards.summary: Group ads by Persona + Angle + Offer so each adset trains on one commercial idea.
cards.use_when: Building adsets or deciding which creatives belong together in a cold campaign.

cards.title: Why 2018-style interest segmentation stopped working
cards.summary: The historical shift from segmented interest structures to consolidating, creative-led buying.
cards.use_when: Understanding why a legacy agency's heavily segmented structure underperforms, or deciding whether to keep many interest adsets.

cards.title: Three settings-style cleanups to audit before restructuring
cards.summary: A reminder to verify interface toggles and default settings before any restructure, plus the non-negotiable principles.
cards.use_when: Preparing a Meta account for restructuring or an audit.

cards.title: Never Touch a Performing Ad Set — Fork It Instead
cards.summary: Preserve winning Meta ad sets untouched and route new creative and new spend into adjacent ad sets and campaigns to protect what already works.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add new ad creative into an existing Meta ad set or spin it into a new one during creative testing or scaling.

cards.title: Exclude Existing Customers and Set 7-Day Click Attribution
cards.summary: Protect ad test integrity by excluding past purchasers from cold campaigns and reading results on 7-day click attribution.
cards.use_when: Configuring audience exclusions and attribution settings before launching cold acquisition campaigns or interpreting their results.

cards.title: Set Test Budgets by Back-Propagating from CPA
cards.summary: Size each ad set test budget as a multiple of target CPA (3x minimum, 5x preferred) so the test reaches a real yes/no decision.
cards.use_when: Setting ad set budgets and kill rules for a new creative concept test in a Meta account.

cards.title: Run Tests One Week to Capture Seasonality and Time-to-Purchase
cards.summary: Set test duration by balancing two forces — daily seasonality and time to purchase — typically landing near one week.
cards.use_when: Choosing how many days to let a creative or concept test run before reading results and making a kill or scale decision.

cards.title: KPI at Ad Set Level and Scale Budgets in 20% Daily Steps
cards.summary: Manage sub-$50k/month accounts by KPI-ing ad sets on target CPA or ROAS and raising winning budgets about 20% per day.
cards.use_when: Running routine optimization in a small Meta ad account where spend volume is too low for heavy campaign segmentation.

cards.title: Keep Account Structure Consolidated at Low Spend
cards.summary: At low spend, consolidate conversions into few campaigns, use structured creative testing, and avoid segmentation you cannot read.
cards.use_when: Designing a Meta account structure for a business spending under roughly $50k per month.

cards.title: Layer Campaigns at $50k–$250k with a Commercial Reason
cards.summary: Add campaigns at mid-scale spend only when each one maps to a funnel, persona, or product with different economics and its own KPI.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add campaigns or ad sets as a store's Meta spend scales from about $50k to $250k per month.

cards.title: Build Creative Concepts as Persona × Angle × Offer × Ad Type
cards.summary: Run a concept matrix so ad sets map to structured concepts and creative output becomes directional rather than random.
cards.use_when: Planning monthly creative production and setting up ad set structure for a Meta account at mid to high spend.

cards.title: Use Concept Testing to Shape Retention and Product Strategy
cards.summary: Concept-level performance tells you who you are acquiring and in what proportions, which should feed retention flows and product expansion.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to route post-purchase retention, win-back and product portfolio decisions based on ad account persona data.

cards.title: Run a Dedicated Promo Campaign to Protect Learning
cards.summary: Segment promotions into their own campaign so repeated promo launches do not disrupt testing and scaling learning.
cards.use_when: Running frequent promotions (the source's example runs every three to four weeks) in a Meta account with active testing and scaling campaigns.

cards.title: Consolidate Website-Visitor Retargeting into Cold Campaigns
cards.summary: For most accounts, skip a dedicated website-visitor retargeting campaign because existing campaigns already reach engaged audiences.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to build a website visitor retargeting campaign for a store's Meta account.

cards.title: Treat Retargeting as a Capped Support Layer
cards.summary: Minimize retargeting spend, consolidate audiences, and watch frequency instead of letting retargeting absorb cold budget.
cards.use_when: Auditing or redesigning retargeting campaigns in a store's Meta account.

cards.title: Read DPA ROAS with 7-Day Click or Incremental Attribution
cards.summary: DPAs sit just before purchase and over-claim credit, so assess them on honest attribution and treat their performance as a mirror of top-of-funnel spend.
cards.use_when: Evaluating dynamic product ad performance and setting DPA budgets in a store with a large catalog, especially fashion.

cards.title: Choose ABO vs CBO by Risk Versus Efficiency Profile
cards.summary: The ABO/CBO question is really a choice between forcing spend through tests and letting the algorithm maximize return — pick per account, season and AOV.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to run ad-set-budget-optimized or campaign-budget-optimized campaigns in a Meta account.

cards.title: Keep Three to Fifteen Ads per Ad Set, Aligned to One Audience
cards.summary: Fill each ad set with multiple ads that sequence to the same audience, consolidating awareness stages rather than splitting them.
cards.use_when: Deciding how many ads to place in each ad set and whether to split awareness stages into separate ad sets.

cards.title: Name Ad Sets by Persona, Angle, Offer and Date
cards.summary: Use a consistent ad set naming convention so you can filter and bundle concept performance across the campaign.
cards.use_when: Setting naming conventions for new ad sets or cleaning up an inherited Meta account with vague names like 'March 7 creatives'.

cards.title: Add a Second Ad Account with Different Bid Logic to Derisk and Expand Auction Entry
cards.summary: Run a parallel ad account on the same pixel with different bidding to reach more auctions and protect against a primary account failure.
cards.use_when: Considering account-level redundancy or additional reach for a store spending roughly $250k+ per month on Meta.

cards.title: Avoid Splitting Ad Accounts by Country
cards.summary: Keep regions in one ad account wherever possible and only split when you need billing in local currency.
cards.use_when: Structuring Meta ad accounts for a store expanding into multiple international markets.

cards.title: Add a Page Strategy Before You Hit Ad Limits
cards.summary: Plan how you will run ads across multiple pages because large accounts will hit page-level ad limits.
cards.use_when: Planning Meta account infrastructure for a store approaching high monthly ad spend.

cards.title: Find the Spend Equilibrium Where Efficiency Breaks
cards.summary: Scale spend on a winner until returns fall below profitability, pull back, and treat the resulting ceiling as that creative's natural spend capacity.
cards.use_when: Setting daily spend ceilings for a winning Meta ad set and deciding when a winner has genuinely maxed out.

cards.title: Budget existing-customer retargeting by dollar and frequency, not percent
cards.summary: Replace 'existing customer spend percentage' with a dollar budget derived from customer count, CPM, and desired monthly frequency, judged on profit and frequency.
cards.use_when: Setting or reviewing retargeting/existing-customer budget allocation in your Meta ad account for a store with a growing customer list.

cards.title: Avoiding the DPA death spiral: protect top-of-funnel investment
cards.summary: Shifting budget from top-of-funnel prospecting into DPAs lifts DPA-reported revenue short-term but starves the funnel and causes account-wide decline; keep top-of-funnel spend and creative throughput protected.
cards.use_when: When DPA/retargeting ROAS looks strong and you're tempted to raise its budget, cut prospecting, or reduce creative production.

cards.title: Turn off Meta flexible ads to preserve creative read-outs
cards.summary: Flexible ads bundle multiple assets into one ad with no visibility into which creative drove results, breaking your data feedback loop; only use them with near-identical assets.
cards.use_when: Deciding ad formats when launching Meta creative tests or trying to work around the account's ad/page limits.

cards.title: Deprioritize cost caps and bid caps below ~$200k/month
cards.summary: Bidding strategy is low-leverage for most sub-$200k/month ad accounts; solve other bottlenecks first and treat cost caps as an advanced lever, not a growth switch.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to spend time testing cost caps or bid caps in a Meta ad account, or when someone proposes bidding changes as the growth plan.

cards.title: Disable 1-day view attribution for budget and scaling decisions
cards.summary: One-day-view attribution over-attributes revenue, especially from existing customers, so exclude it from adset budget-flow and scaling decisions.
cards.use_when: Reviewing Meta reporting to decide which adsets to scale, cut, or shift budget between.

cards.title: Turn off Advantage+ creative optimizations at account and ad level
cards.summary: Advantage+ creative optimizations re-enable themselves over time unless you disable them in advertiser settings, so turn them off at both account and individual ad level to keep creative testing clean.
cards.use_when: Auditing Meta ad account setup before launching creative tests, or when creative settings keep reverting unexpectedly.

cards.title: Audit audience segment syncs to prevent existing customers being served as new
cards.summary: Broken audience-segment syncs (e.g. Klaviyo to Meta) cause existing customers to be targeted as new, eroding data integrity and wasting spend.
cards.use_when: Routine ad-account audits or when existing-customer/new-customer reporting looks inconsistent with your CRM or email platform.

cards.title: Size test budgets from target conversions, CPA, and duration
cards.summary: Calculate a test's daily budget as (target conversions × expected CPA) ÷ test duration in days, choosing the conversion threshold and learning speed explicitly before launch.
cards.use_when: Planning any Meta ad test (creative concept, audience, structure) and needing to know how much to spend and for how long.

cards.title: Four-question checklist to validate any ad account structure
cards.summary: Judge account structure by whether it produces readable data, matches how the business makes profit, fits your spend/creative tier, and sizes support layers to actual retention.
cards.use_when: Designing a new Meta account structure or auditing an existing one, especially after scaling spend or changing creative output.

cards.title: Review the whole ad account at once when auditing spend allocation
cards.summary: Don't evaluate one adset or campaign in isolation; audit spend allocation across all campaigns and support layers to spot problems like top-of-funnel starvation or DPA over-weighting.
cards.use_when: Running an audit of a store's Meta ad account, or diagnosing declining account performance when individual campaigns look fine.

cards.title: Meta's four-step ad serving pipeline
cards.summary: Retrieval, light ranking, heavy ranking and auction are the four stages Meta runs in roughly 200ms to pick which ad serves to a user.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why a new ad gets no delivery, or setting expectations for how long creative needs to prove itself before you judge it.

cards.title: The Total Value equation behind every winning impression
cards.summary: Meta's Total Value equals (advertiser bid x estimated action rate) plus user value, so improving CTR and funnel conversion raises your effective bid without raising your bid.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to raise bids or fix creative and post-click conversion when an ad set cannot spend or CPA is too high.

cards.title: Creative is the targeting: broad targeting after Andromeda
cards.summary: Meta now reads creative elements to determine audience, making heavy manual interest and lookalike audience structures largely redundant for most ecommerce accounts.
cards.use_when: Structuring a new Meta ad account or rebuilding a legacy one built on stacks of interest and lookalike audiences.

cards.title: Andromeda changed retrieval, not the value of variations
cards.summary: The Andromeda update to retrieval made Meta lean harder on creative for targeting, but variations within a concept remain the highest-leverage way to get more at-bats.
cards.use_when: Planning a creative testing roadmap and deciding how many net-new concepts versus variations to launch each week.

cards.title: Choosing auto-bidding versus cost caps and bid caps
cards.summary: Lowest-cost auto bidding and manual cost or bid caps both run profitable accounts at very high spend, so pick the method that solves your actual constraint.
cards.use_when: Deciding bidding strategy for a new campaign or when a stalled ad set needs a different bidding lever.

cards.title: Stop optimizing to leave the learning phase
cards.summary: Ads keep learning for their whole life, so rule on 7-day and longer windows of spend instead of reacting to daily swings, especially at low budgets.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to kill an ad or ad set after volatile daily ROAS, particularly in accounts spending under about $1,000 per day.
